questions.text: Are the business's recurring operating activities defined so they are performed the same way each time?

A.text: Activities are performed differently depending on who does them; nothing is defined

B.text: Some activities are defined informally — in people's heads or scattered notes

C.text: The most important recurring activities are defined and written down

D.text: As C, and they are followed in practice rather than only documented

E.text: As D, and they are kept current — reviewed and updated when the business changes how it works

questions.text: Does the business have the capacity — people, equipment, facilities, or time — to meet what it has committed to, and does it manage that capacity forward?

A.text: Capacity is regularly insufficient; commitments are missed, or met only through unsustainable effort

B.text: Capacity roughly matches commitments but is not planned; pressure is discovered when it arrives

C.text: Capacity meets current commitments and is monitored, so pressure becomes visible before it is acute

D.text: As C, and capacity is planned forward against expected demand, with the lead time to add it understood

E.text: As D, and the business holds headroom or a defined means of adding capacity quickly enough to absorb a material increase without failing commitments

questions.text: How does the business manage the suppliers, providers, or inputs it depends on?

A.text: Dependencies are not identified; disruption to a supplier or provider would be discovered when it happened

B.text: Dependencies are known informally; no alternatives have been identified

C.text: Critical dependencies are identified, and their terms and reliability are understood

D.text: As C, and alternatives have been identified for the critical ones, or the relationship is secured — contract, agreed terms, held stock, or equivalent

E.text: As D, and the arrangement has been tested or the alternative used, so it is known to work rather than assumed

questions.text: Does the business deliver what it commits to, when and how it committed?

A.text: Missed commitments are a normal occurrence rather than an exception

B.text: Commitments are usually met, but through individual effort and rework rather than reliable process

C.text: Commitments are met consistently; failures are the exception

D.text: As C, and failures are recorded and their causes identified

E.text: As D, and causes are addressed so the same failure does not recur, with evidence this is working

questions.text: If a significant disruption occurred — loss of a facility, a system, a key supplier, or access to a location — how prepared is the business to continue?

A.text: No consideration has been given to it

B.text: The risks are recognised but nothing is prepared

C.text: The most significant disruptions have been identified and basic protections exist — backups, insurance, alternative arrangements

D.text: As C, and a defined plan exists for continuing or recovering operations

E.text: As D, and the plan has been tested or used rather than assumed to work
